evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check is based only on positive and differing manager PIDs and invocation IDs. A guest reboot between the manager before/after probes can change both identifiers, satisfying this check even if the manager itself did not restart. The separate `boot_id_changed` check is tied to `reboot.get(...)`, so it does not constrain `manager_restarted`. Requiring equal, nonempty boot IDs on the manager before/after observations is a minimal correctness repair.
